* At least 150 people die in [[Kinshasa]], [[Democratic Republic of Congo]] in fighting between the military and forces loyal to [[Senate of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|Senator]] [[Jean-Pierre Bemba]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/africa/6492283.stm (BBC)]
* The United Kingdom announces the withdrawal of all [[British Armed Forces]] serving as part of the [[European Union Force]] in [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/6491749.stm (BBC)]
* [[Iraq War]]: At least 47 people die in [[Iraqi civil war (2006–2008)|insurgent]] strikes including 20 as a result of a [[suicide attack|suicide]] [[car bomb|truck bomb]] in a [[Baghdad]] police station. [http://www.guardian.co.uk/worldlatest/story/0,,-6505933,00.html (AP via The Guardian)]
* The [[United Nations Security Council]] unanimously adopts [[United Nations Security Council Resolution 1747|Resolution 1747]], imposing additional [[economic sanction]]s on the [[Islamic Republic of Iran]] for its ongoing [[Nuclear programme of Iran|nuclear programme]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/03/24/AR2007032400576.html (Washington Post)]
* [[Xi Jinping]] is appointed the new [[Politics of Shanghai|CPC Shanghai Committee Secretary]], thus becoming the number one figure in Shanghai, replacing acting party chief [[Han Zheng]]. He leaves his post as Party chief in [[Zhejiang]]. [http://news.xinhuanet.com/local/2007-03/24/content_5890690.htm (Xinhua)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2007/03/25/world/asia/25china.html (New York Times)]
* [[New South Wales state election, 2007|Elections]] in the Australian state of [[New South Wales]] sees the [[Australian Labor Party]] led by [[Morris Iemma]] retain government despite a small swing against it.
